nodes.name: When Called
nodes.notes: ADR-052 Block 4b. gpt-image-2 reference (image-to-image) edit leg, called per-request by Generate Images Parallel for ref_transport==='edits'. Inputs: placeholder_id (echoed back for caller correlation), prompt, size (gpt-valid, snapped upstream), reference_url (first resolved reference). Returns {placeholder_id, ok, b64_json, header_cost, statusCode, error}. The multipart /v1/images/edits transport (Block 0 proven) CANNOT run in a Code node (n8n httpRequest corrupts a raw multipart Buffer -> LiteLLM 400 'Too many fields'); only the dedicated HTTP Request node serialises it.

nodes.name: Get Image Key
nodes.notes: Reads the dedicated, revocable LiteLLM image key from Supabase Vault via public.get_litellm_image_key() (migration 032), same getter the batch uses. HTTP nodes can't use credentials and $env/$vars are blocked, so a credentialed Postgres read is how this leg gets the secret to Bearer-auth the edits call. NO onError: a missing key throws -> the caller's executeWorkflow onError fails soft to plain gen, whose own key check CRITICALs (auth broken = real failure, surfaced via the batch).

nodes.name: Download Reference
nodes.notes: Download the reference image bytes to binary property `data` (responseFormat file -> no base64 in JSON; off-heap under binaryMode separate). Reference URLs are pre-signed (ClickUp / Supabase signed), so no auth header. Mirrors read-input's Fetch Attachment Binary. continueRegularOutput + retry: a dead/404 ref URL leaves no binary, so Edit Call yields no b64 and Shape b64 returns ok:false -> caller fails soft to plain gen (never throws/CRITICAL). Block 5: alwaysOutputData so a failed download still emits an item (no binary) -> the chain reaches Shape b64, which reads this node's binary presence to classify fail_kind='fetch'.

nodes.name: Edit Call
nodes.notes: ADR-052 Block 0/4b: gpt-image-2 reference transport. POST http://litellm:4000/v1/images/edits as multipart/form-data: image=reference binary (formBinaryData, inputDataFieldName data), model=openai/gpt-image-2, prompt, size, n=1. Bearer = Vault image key. fullResponse=true to read x-litellm-response-cost; neverError=true so a 4xx/5xx returns the body (Shape b64 detects no-b64 -> ok:false, not a throw). The HTTP Request node assembles multipart in n8n's own runtime, sidestepping the Code-node form-data block. Returns image at data[0].b64_json (raw base64, NOT a data URI). onError continueRegularOutput is a network-failure backstop.

nodes.name: Shape b64
nodes.notes: SOLE TERMINAL (sub-workflow return determinism): single linear chain, one leaf. Parses the Edit Call full response -> {placeholder_id (echoed for caller correlation), ok, b64_json (data[0].b64_json), header_cost (x-litellm-response-cost; treat as unreliable per Block 0 -> caller keeps the price floor), statusCode, error}. ok:false (no b64 / non-2xx / network fail) tells the caller to fail soft to plain text-to-image. Never throws. ADR-052 Block 5: also returns fail_kind — 'fetch' (no binary reached Edit Call -> the reference URL couldn't be downloaded), 'oversize' (edit error body indicates the image is too large), or 'edit' (generic edit rejection) — so the batch can emit a distinct, actionable WARN per failure mode.
